name: Disabling database security/integrity controls
attack_scenario: A migration disables RLS on a multi-tenant table and never re-enables it; every tenant's queries now return all tenants' rows, turning a routine deploy into a mass data-exposure breach.
negative_test_hint: submit the migration statement "ALTER TABLE tenants DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;" and assert the review or migration tooling rejects it instead of applying it

exemplar.noncompliant: ALTER TABLE accounts DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
exemplar.compliant: ALTER TABLE accounts ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
exemplar.explanation: These statements switch off tenant isolation (RLS), referential/uniqueness integrity (FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0, UNIQUE_CHECKS=0, NOCHECK CONSTRAINT) or audit/enforcement triggers (DISABLE TRIGGER ALL, session_replication_role=replica). Left in a shipped script they let inconsistent or cross-tenant data land permanently, so security and integrity controls must stay enabled in production schema changes.
